tagline: Twists through Kentucky hills link Mammoth Cave country with Tennessee
intro: The Cordell Hull Highway winds through hills and valleys between the entrance to Mammoth Cave National Park and the Tennessee border. The National Scenic Byway Foundation presents this Kentucky state byway as a drive of twists and turns, with Old Mulkey Meetinghouse as a historic stop near its southern end. Its published length is 51.6 miles.

Kentucky designated the corridor on May 24, 1995, joining sections of several numbered highways under the Cordell Hull name. Hull was born in a Tennessee log cabin and became the longest-serving U.S. secretary of state. His work toward establishing the United Nations earned him the Nobel Peace Prize in 1945.

Begin at the park entrance on KY 255, then follow the corridor along KY 70 and KY 90 toward Glasgow. Cave City comes before Glasgow, with the two towns connected by KY 90. On KY 63, Temple Hill sits at the junction with KY 1324, and Mud Lick lies farther toward Tompkinsville at KY 870. From Glasgow, KY 63 leads to Tompkinsville; the designated route continues through Monroe County using KY 63, KY 100 and KY 163 to reach Tennessee. Old Mulkey Meetinghouse adds a stop near the border, where Daniel Boone’s sister Hannah is buried.

moments.title: Cave City
moments.text: Cave City takes its name from a cave within the town limits, whose creek supplied water to the Louisville & Nashville Railroad. The Knob City Land Company bought the town site in 1853 with plans for a resort serving nearby Mammoth Cave. The company laid out main streets 80 feet wide as it began selling lots. The first train arrived in 1859. During the passenger-rail era, tourists left the trains here and transferred to transportation to the cave. Tourism remains the city’s main industry, with Mammoth Cave National Park ten miles west via KY 70.

moments.title: Glasgow
moments.text: A large spring and land for public buildings helped make Glasgow a county seat in 1799. John Gorin donated 50 acres, and the town’s central location also weighed in its selection. Its name came from the Scottish hometown of the father of William Logan, one of the commissioners choosing the county seat. Glasgow holds annual Scottish Highland Games. South Green Street offers another way to read the town’s past: its historic houses include Colonial, Federal and Victorian styles. The houses across Glasgow reach back to the early 1800s, with South Green Street a concentration of different architectural styles.

moments.title: Old Mulkey Meetinghouse
moments.text: Twelve corners give Old Mulkey Meetinghouse the shape of a cross, while three doors symbolize the Holy Trinity. Built in 1804 during a religious revival, it is Kentucky’s oldest log meetinghouse. The congregation began as Mill Creek Baptist Church, founded by Baptists from North and South Carolina under Philip Mulkey’s leadership. The church and adjacent cemetery became part of the state park system in 1931. Revolutionary War soldiers are buried here, as is Hannah Boone, Daniel Boone’s sister. The meetinghouse and cemetery occupy a 20-acre state historic site in Monroe County, Kentucky.
moments.notice: Look for the cross-shaped plan with twelve corners and three doors.
